chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Outdrawing the rival club; Benny Waters and Kansas Fields
summary: Butler's club was full every night while a bop rival across town had no business; his band included multi-instrumentalist Benny Waters and drummer Kansas Fields.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, because you had some -- I didn't play this too much here, because there was a fellow across town playing that, and he had no business. And I had all the business.
Who was the cat across town?
Well, I tell you, it was a place called the "Chaque Perche" (PHONETIC).
Oh, yeah, that's existed for a long time.

Yeah, Chaque et Pische. But see, I was full every night. And I stayed there and took his business, and was getting them calls, and things. In fact, I didn't have to go to the Champs Elysees, sometimes it would be months before I'd go to the Champs Elysees, because too much was happening up at my kingdom. There was so much happening at Pigalle.
So I had a fellow named Benny Waters (PHONETIC). Now, he was a champ. Benny Waters is an old musician. Right now he'd be about 76, right now.
Let me turn this tape over.
Benny Waters plays the piano and he
plays all the saxophones and he loves those saxophones. And we went very well together. I had Kansas Fields on the drums but -- I don't know, he wasn't even with me.
Now, what year are we talking about now?
